name: @finapp/m36-events
description: M36 — Webhooks & Event Streaming (Stage 6D-4, mvp:false): the governed OUTBOUND fan-out layer over the platform's domain events — external webhook ENDPOINTS, event SUBSCRIPTIONS/filters, webhook DELIVERY evidence, and tenant event STREAMS with consumer CURSORS. THE LOAD-BEARING BOUNDARY: m06 owns THE ONE event-delivery path/outbox (ADR-004) — m36 is NOT a second outbox or a second internal delivery path; it CONSUMES domain events by contract (through a fail-closed EventSourcePort fed by the m06 outbox dispatcher) and fans them out to governed external subscribers, recording each delivery attempt. Webhook delivery is EXTERNAL EGRESS: it is FRAMEWORK ONLY behind a fail-closed WebhookDeliveryPort (deterministic offline doubles, NO production network/provider, allow-listed endpoint URLs only — an unavailable runtime yields a durable BLOCKED outcome). NOT a secrets manager: an endpoint's signing secret is an opaque secretref: pointer (the m30 seam); ZERO secret VALUE columns; real key mgmt = m41 behind a fail-closed port. Registering/activating an external endpoint (that egresses tenant data) is a CONTROLLED action (maker-checker/SoD, AI never approves, default deny). It uses the webhook_*/eventstream_*/events_* table prefixes (integration_* is m23's, connector_* is m33's, marketplace_* is m34's, devportal_* is m35's) and owns webhook.lifecycle + eventstream.lifecycle ONLY. Declares /api/v1/webhooks + /api/v1/events, the events.* permission namespace (GAP-4 resolved), the two event families (published through the ONE m06 outbox) and the WEBHOOK_/EVENTSTREAM_ audit prefixes. Delivery is idempotent; a subscriber receives only its own tenant's events (FORCE-RLS). No secret value; no external network/provider; no arbitrary code.
